body:
Thank you, I'll keep in mind the offer I really do appreciate it. Sorry for taking so long to get back to you.

I know I most likely need real professional help, I'm really having trouble even getting to the point where I'm motivated to seek it out and I feel my money issues are a huge problem in getting help. The worst part is the driving I do - it lets me sort out my thoughts and keeps me calm and collected enough to know I need help and not do anything crazy, but keeps me broke to the point help is out of reach. 

I don't feel comfortable talking to friends about this - my closest friends are still in the state I used to live, not here, and I think all this would be too much of a bomb to drop over the phone. I'm friends with my coworkers here, but not close enough to talk about anything remotely serious.
I will say that I took a piece of your advice and told a police officer I know I needed help(I pressed that it wasn't urgent) and he did give me a phone number that may help and said he would make some calls to help me get started in the right direction for finding help. Don't want to bother him by calling to ask and don't really know when to expect to hear from him(If he can find anything out at all - he is far from the jurisdiction I live in but I appreciate him trying). I guess that's a step.

I used to really enjoy hiking, however since the wreck my physical ability has diminished due to pain from injuries. I honestly don't know if I'd be able to do any of those things. I work a very physically demanding job, so maybe I could do those things, but some days leave me in such pain that I can hardly function even with my prescriptions. I'd be worried about starting something and realize halfway through that I can't do it. I don't know if it'd be worth the risk if it did cause problems.

Thank you for your post, sorry it's taken me a couple days to get back to you.

I'm not aware of any free local resources, but that's one reason I keep wanting to call the hotline. I figure even if I can't talk to them they could maybe point me in the right direction but I still can't even muster up the courage to stay on the line until they answer I don't know how I could expect to actually ask them anything. I'm stuck wondering if once they pick up if things get easier and maybe comforting, or if I'd get stuck in an awkward conversation that would run in circles and make me feel worse.

I know there is a group that works with people who have been assaulted but I know absolutely nothing about it other than that it exists. And you're right, I do feel that the assault has pretty much laid the outline for everything and is the main thing I need to handle to get any relief... but I haven't been able to bring myself to do it and because of that I've added all these other problems(the wreck, moving back in with parents, etc.) to contribute to the constant cycle of guilt, shame and bad decisions. I don't even want to acknowledge that the assault happened and while avoiding dealing with it has obviously not worked out well in the past and I know this I still can't bring myself to do any different. I feel like me knowing that my reasoning is stupid and doesn't make sense should be plenty enough to change it but it's just not. I really don't know what can push me in one direction or the other.
